ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AB$ is the diameter of circle $O$. Points $C$ and $D$ are on circle $O$, and segments $AC$, $BC$, and $CD$ are connected respectively. Given that $\angle DOB=150^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle ACD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle DOB=150^\circ$ and $\angle AOD+\angle DOB=180^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle AOD=30^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle ACD=\frac{1}{2}\angle AOD=15^\circ$.\\
Therefore, the answer is: $\boxed{15^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle, AB is a horizontal diameter, and the center O is on AB; A is on the left side of the circle, B is on the right side of the circle, C is on the upper arc, and D is on the lower-left arc; AC, BC, and CD are connected, and it can be seen that OD and OB form the central angle ∠DOB. Reasoning: It is known that ∠DOB = 150°. Because AB is a diameter, OA and OB are opposite rays on the same straight line, so ∠AOD = 180° - 150° = 30°. The degree measure of the minor arc AD corresponding to the central angle ∠AOD is 30°. ∠ACD is an inscribed angle, and what it intercepts is exactly arc AD, so ∠ACD equals half of the intercepted arc, namely 30° ÷ 2 = 15°.
